name: algo-pseudocode-fahem
_comment: Original grammar written for Fahem, covering only chapter-1 syntax that
is actually pinned or corpus-verified (see the coverage report in
context.py's PINS / chunks.json). Not derived from, or structurally
modeled on, any third-party grammar - written from scratch against
Fahem's own material.
Deliberately excluded: control-structure keywords (si/alors/sinon,
pour/tant que/repeter/selon, retourner, algorithme/fonction/procedure,
ouvrir/fermer/fin_fichier, enregistrement, ouex). These are not real
chapter-1 syntax per the coverage report, and generate.py's own
CONTROL_STRUCTURES checker treats them as violations when invented.
Leaving them unmatched here means they render as plain text - coloring
them as legitimate syntax would visually contradict what the checker
enforces. See CROSS_CHECK_NOTES.md alongside this file.
Boundary convention: a token is bounded by lookaround rather than \b,
because JS \w is ASCII-only and these identifiers carry accented
letters (Écrire, sous_chaîne, racine_carrée). BOUND excludes
[A-Za-z\u00C0-\u00FF_] on both sides so a match can't start or end
mid-identifier (e.g. 'lire' inside 'Lire_ligne').
Function-name categories additionally require a following '(' via a
zero-width lookahead, so a token only lights up when actually called -
reduces accidental matches and mirrors how every one of these appears
in the corpus (always as Nom(...), never as a bare word).

io-functions.comment: Compound names (écrire_nl, lire_ligne) must be tried before the plain écrire/lire so the plainer pattern doesn't win at the same start position and leave '_nl'/'_ligne' unmatched. écrire_nl/lire_ligne are not in the chapter-1 corpus - included per project owner: confirmed real bac-curriculum syntax, chapter not yet ingested.

types.comment: NOT included in the active `patterns` list above - disabled after real testing showed why. Type words (entier, réel...) never legitimately appear in the Algorithme column of the solution table this grammar is applied to; they live in the separate Objet|Nature/type declaration table, which this grammar never touches. Verified in the browser: a generated answer's own message string - 'Ecrire ("Entrez le premier entier")' - contains the ordinary French word 'entier' as prose, and with this category active it lit up as if it were a type declaration. Bare-word matching with no code-context guard can't tell 'entier' the type from 'entier' the adjective, so this category does more harm than good here. Left in the repository, unused, in case a future task also wraps the declaration table, where these patterns would be correct.
